practiceQuestions.q: Which article of the Indian Constitution provides for the abolition or creation of Legislative Councils in states?
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 169 empowers Parliament to create or abolish a Legislative Council if the Legislative Assembly of the state passes a resolution to that effect by a special majority. Article 168 deals with the constitution of legislatures in states, Article 170 with the composition of Assemblies, and Article 171 with the composition of Councils.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the maximum permissible strength of a State Legislative Council as a proportion of the State Legislative Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: According to Article 171, the total number of members in the Legislative Council of a state shall not exceed one-third of the total number of members in the Legislative Assembly of that state.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum permissible strength of a State Legislative Council under the Indian Constitution?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 171(1), the minimum strength of a State Legislative Council is fixed at 40 members (except in certain historical exceptions, though 40 is the constitutional floor).

practiceQuestions.q: What is the tenure of a member of the State Legislative Council (MLC)?
practiceQuestions.sol: Like the Rajya Sabha at the Centre, the Legislative Council is a permanent body not subject to dissolution. However, one-third of its members retire every second year, giving individual MLCs a tenure of 6 years.

practiceQuestions.q: What proportion of Legislative Council members are elected by the members of the State Legislative Assembly?
practiceQuestions.sol: One-third (1/3rd) of the total members of the Legislative Council are elected by the members of the Legislative Assembly from amongst persons who are not members of the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q: Who nominates the members of the Legislative Council who possess special knowledge or practical experience in literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service?
practiceQuestions.sol: One-sixth (1/6th) of the total members are nominated by the Governor of the state from persons having special knowledge or practical experience in fields such as literature, science, art, cooperative movement, and social service.

practiceQuestions.q: Which of the following Indian states currently does NOT have a Legislative Council?
practiceQuestions.sol: As of now, only 6 states have Legislative Councils: Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Maharashtra, and Karnataka. Madhya Pradesh does not have one, though provisions were made in the 1956 Act.

practiceQuestions.q: What proportion of Legislative Council members are elected by electorates consisting of local authorities such as municipalities, district boards, etc.?
practiceQuestions.sol: One-third (1/3rd) of the members are elected by local authorities like municipalities, district boards, cantonment boards, and other notified local bodies in the state.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the minimum age requirement for a person to become a member of the State Legislative Council?
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 173(b), the minimum age for contesting or being chosen as a member of the Legislative Council is 30 years (same as Rajya Sabha), while for the Legislative Assembly it is 25 years.

practiceQuestions.q: A Money Bill can be introduced in which house of the State Legislature?
opts: Either house of the State Legislature
practiceQuestions.sol: A Money Bill can only be introduced in the Legislative Assembly and not in the Legislative Council, mirroring the Lok Sabha-Rajya Sabha dynamic at the Centre.

practiceQuestions.q: Why is the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council under Article 169 not considered a constitutional amendment under Article 368?
opts: Because it requires ratification by all state legislatures.
Because the Constitution explicitly states that such law shall not be deemed for the purposes of Article 368.
Because it is done purely through an executive order of the Governor.
Because the Supreme Court declared it an ordinary legislative act.
practiceQuestions.sol: Article 169(4) explicitly specifies that any law passed for the creation or abolition of a Legislative Council shall not be deemed to be an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368. It can be passed by Parliament by a simple majority.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the power of the State Legislative Council regarding ordinary bills compare with that of the Rajya Sabha at the national level?
opts: Legislative Council has absolute veto power, unlike Rajya Sabha.
Legislative Council is much weaker; it can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum of 4 months, whereas Rajya Sabha can delay it for 6 months.
Both have co-equal powers in passing all types of legislation.
Joint sittings are provisioned for states to resolve deadlocks, just like the Parliament.
practiceQuestions.sol: Unlike Parliament where a joint sitting resolves deadlocks (and Rajya Sabha can delay a bill for 6 months), the State Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill for a maximum of 4 months (3 months in first instance, 1 month subsequently). Furthermore, there is NO provision for a joint sitting of the two houses of a state legislature.

practiceQuestions.q: Why are graduates and teachers given separate representation in the State Legislative Council?
opts: To ensure functional representation of educated and intellectual classes in governance.
Because they fund the elections of the Legislative Council.
As a reward for their contribution during the freedom struggle.
To bypass the influence of political parties entirely.
practiceQuestions.sol: The framers of the Constitution incorporated functional representation into the Legislative Council, allotting 1/12th of the seats to graduates of at least 3 years standing and 1/12th to teachers of educational institutions not lower than secondary schools.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the role of the State Legislative Council in the election of the President of India?
opts: MLCs participate along with MLAs in the Electoral College.
MLCs are strictly excluded from the Electoral College for the President's election.
Only nominated MLCs can vote in the presidential election.
MLCs hold casting votes in case of a tie in the presidential poll.
practiceQuestions.sol: Under Article 54, the Electoral College for the President consists of elected members of both Houses of Parliament and elected members of the State Legislative Assemblies. Members of Legislative Councils (MLCs) do NOT participate in the presidential election.

practiceQuestions.q: Consider the relationship between the Legislative Assembly and the Legislative Council regarding a non-money bill. If the Assembly rejects the amendments suggested by the Council, what happens?
opts: The Assembly can pass the bill again and send it to the Council, and after 1 month, the bill is deemed passed even if the Council rejects it again.
The Governor must dissolve the Assembly.
The matter goes to the Supreme Court for arbitration.
practiceQuestions.sol: The ultimate power lies with the Legislative Assembly. If the Council rejects a bill passed by the Assembly, or passes it with unacceptable amendments, or does not pass it within 3 months, the Assembly can pass it a second time and send it to the Council. If the Council then rejects it or sits on it for 1 month, the bill is deemed passed by both houses in the form it was passed by the Assembly the second time.

practiceQuestions.q: Why do critics argue that the State Legislative Council is often a 'white elephant' or a redundant house?
opts: Because it frequently blocks progressive legislation passed by directly elected representatives.
Because it has very limited delaying powers, incurs high financial costs, and often serves as a back door for defeated politicians.
Because its members are appointed directly by the Prime Minister.
Because it is unconstitutional under the basic structure doctrine.
practiceQuestions.sol: Critics point out that the Legislative Council acts as a mere revising body with weak powers, strains the state exchequer financially, and is often exploited to rehabilitate politicians who lost assembly elections.

practiceQuestions.q: How are casual vacancies in the Legislative Council filled?
opts: By direct nomination by the Chief Minister for the full 6-year term.
Through by-elections for the remainder of the predecessor's term.
They remain vacant until the next general assembly election.
By appointing an MLA from the ruling party temporarily.
practiceQuestions.sol: A member elected or nominated to fill a casual vacancy holds office only for the remainder of the term of the member whom they replace, through a by-election conducted for that specific constituency/category.

practiceQuestions.q: What is the constitutional position of the State Legislative Council regarding Constitutional Amendment Bills passed by Parliament that require state ratification under Article 368?
opts: The Legislative Council must approve it independently before the Assembly's resolution is valid.
Constitutional amendments do not require state legislature approval at all.
Ratification is a joint act of the state legislature, and if there is disagreement between the two houses, the view of the Legislative Assembly prevails.
Only the Legislative Council has the power to ratify national constitutional amendments.
practiceQuestions.sol: When a constitutional amendment bill is referred to states for ratification under Article 368, it must be approved by the state legislature. In case of bicameral states, both houses must pass it, but if there's a deadlock, the Assembly's decision prevails as it is the primary representative house.

practiceQuestions.q: Why does the founding debate in the Constituent Assembly reflect deep skepticism towards the creation of Legislative Councils?
opts: Because members felt it was an undemocratic body that delayed progressive laws and served vested interests.
Because it was directly copied from the American Presidential system.
Because Mahatma Gandhi strictly prohibited bicameralism in states.
Because India lacked sufficient population to sustain two houses.
practiceQuestions.sol: Many members in the Constituent Assembly viewed Legislative Councils as unnecessary, expensive, and reactionary bodies that could thwart popular mandates. Consequently, a compromise was reached leaving their creation/abolition entirely up to the states and Parliament via Article 169.

practiceQuestions.q: How does the composition formula of the Legislative Council ensure a mix of expertise and popular representation?
opts: By equal allocation of seats to all political parties.
By dividing seats among local bodies, graduates, teachers, MLAs, and gubernatorial nominees.
By direct universal adult suffrage for all 100% of seats.
By appointing judges of the High Court to occupy one-half of the seats.
practiceQuestions.sol: The composition of the Council under Article 171(3) is a unique blend: 1/3 by local bodies, 1/3 by MLAs, 1/12 by graduates, 1/12 by teachers, and 1/6 nominated by the Governor, balancing grassroots administration, academic expertise, and political representation.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the creation and abolition of the State Legislative Council:
1. Parliament can create or abolish a Legislative Council only if the state Legislative Assembly passes a resolution to that effect by a simple majority.
2. An Act of Parliament under Article 169 is treated as a constitutional amendment under Article 368.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the state Legislative Assembly must pass the resolution by a *special majority* (i.e., a majority of the total membership of the assembly and a majority of not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting), not a simple majority. Statement 2 is incorrect because Article 169(4) explicitly states that such an Act shall NOT be deemed an amendment of the Constitution for the purposes of Article 368.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements about the composition of the State Legislative Council:
1. One-third of its members are elected by electorates consisting of municipalities, district boards, and other local authorities.
2. One-sixth of its members are elected by teachers of educational institutions not lower than secondary schools in the state.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: 1/3rd are elected by local authorities. Statement 2 is incorrect because teachers elect 1/12th (one-twelfth) of the members, not one-sixth (1/6th). 1/6th members are nominated by the Governor.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the powers of the Legislative Council over Ordinary Bills:
1. The Legislative Council can detain an ordinary bill passed by the Assembly for a maximum period of six months.
2. There is no provision for a joint sitting of the two houses of the state legislature to resolve a deadlock.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the maximum period the Legislative Council can delay an ordinary bill is 4 months in total (3 months in the first instance and 1 month upon re-introduction). Statement 2 is correct: unlike Parliament under Article 108, the Indian Constitution does NOT provide for a joint sitting of the state Assembly and Council.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding Money Bills in relation to the State Legislative Council:
1. A Money Bill can be introduced in the Legislative Council if recommended by the Governor.
2. The Legislative Council has 14 days to return a Money Bill to the Assembly with or without recommendations.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because a Money Bill can ONLY be introduced in the Legislative Assembly, never in the Council. Statement 2 is correct: the Council must return the Money Bill within 14 days of its receipt, and its recommendations are non-binding on the Assembly.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the qualifications and tenure of MLCs:
1. The minimum age for membership of the Legislative Council is 25 years.
2. The Legislative Council is not subject to dissolution, but one-third of its members retire every two years.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the minimum age for the Legislative Council is 30 years (25 years is for the Legislative Assembly). Statement 2 is correct: the Council is a permanent house, and 1/3rd of its members retire every 2 years.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Legislative Council:
1. The Chairman of the Legislative Council is appointed directly by the President of India.
2. The Legislative Council elects two of its members to be respectively Chairman and Deputy Chairman.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Chairman is NOT appointed by the President. Statement 2 is correct: under Article 182, the Legislative Council chooses its own members to be Chairman and Deputy Chairman.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the comparative power of the Assembly and Council in financial matters:
1. The Legislative Council can vote on demands for grants submitted to the state legislature.
2. The budget of the state is presented in both houses simultaneously.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Both statements are incorrect. The estimates of expenditure (budget) are laid before the Assembly, and demands for grants are voted ONLY in the Legislative Assembly, not in the Legislative Council. The Council has no power to vote on demands for grants.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the ordinance-making power and the Legislative Council:
1. Ordinances promulgated by the Governor must be approved by the Legislative Council (if it exists) within six weeks of reassembly.
2. The Legislative Council alone can recommend the promulgation of an ordinance to the Governor.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: ordinances issued by the Governor under Article 213 must be approved by both houses of the state legislature (in bicameral states) within 6 weeks of reassembly. Statement 2 is incorrect because ordinances are promulgated on the aid and advice of the Council of Ministers headed by the Chief Minister, not on the recommendation of the Legislative Council.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the abolition of Legislative Councils in Indian states post-independence:
1. Andhra Pradesh abolished its Legislative Council in 1985 and subsequently re-established it in 2007.
2. Tamil Nadu has never had a Legislative Council in its legislative history.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is correct: Andhra Pradesh abolished its council in 1985 and reconstituted it in 2007. Statement 2 is incorrect because Tamil Nadu *did* have a Legislative Council, which was abolished in 1986.

practiceQuestions.q:
Consider the following statements regarding the control of the Legislative Council over the Council of Ministers:
1. The Legislative Council can move and pass a No-Confidence Motion against the State Council of Ministers.
2. Ministers are collectively responsible only to the State Legislative Assembly, not to the Legislative Council.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
practiceQuestions.sol: Statement 1 is incorrect because the Legislative Council CANNOT move or pass a no-confidence motion against the ministry. Statement 2 is correct: under Article 164(2), the Council of Ministers is collectively responsible solely to the Legislative Assembly, mirroring the Lok Sabha-executive relationship at the Centre.
